This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 25 May '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent PAGASA forecasts for Metro Manila point to a high near 31–35°C on May 25 amid the transition from the dry to the early southwest monsoon season, with scattered afternoon thunderstorms and 30–60% rain chances likely capping daytime peaks through increased cloud cover and evaporative cooling. Model guidance shows modest spread, with some ensembles favoring isolated clearing that could allow readings to reach 36°C while others emphasize persistent moisture limiting maxima closer to 35°C. These near-term conditions, set against May’s climatological average high of roughly 34°C, explain the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 36°C and 37°C as traders weigh the balance between typical heat and convective suppression.
